summary: Open-source RAG and agent app for chatting with your own knowledge base, deployable fully offline with local models.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Langchain-Chatchat (formerly Langchain-ChatGLM) is an open-source RAG and agent application built on LangChain and models such as ChatGLM, Qwen and Llama. It gives you knowledge-base Q&A that can be deployed offline and privately, with strong support for Chinese.
sixtySeconds.problem: Many teams want document Q&A without sending data to the cloud. Chatchat runs with local model frameworks like Xinference, Ollama or LocalAI, and also supports the OpenAI API.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a mature, Apache-2.0 RAG app with a pip install, yaml configuration and support for many local model frameworks.
requirements: A model framework such as Xinference, Ollama or LocalAI running your LLM and embedding models

overview: Since 0.3.0 it installs as a Python library, and it no longer loads models from local paths. Start a model framework (the README uses Xinference as the example) with your LLM and embedding models first, ideally in a separate virtual environment.

Run chatchat init to create data folders, copy the sample knowledge base and generate yaml config files. Set your models in model_settings.yaml, then build the knowledge base with chatchat kb -r and start everything with chatchat start -a.
Docker images exist and docker-compose is recommended for Docker deployments. The project is Apache 2.0 licensed.
limitations: You run a separate model framework
Main docs are in Chinese; the English README is older
